root_cause.text: In netfilter's `ip6t_eui64` matcher, `eui64_mt6()` incorrectly tied MAC-header validation to `par->fragoff != 0`, allowing packets with `fragoff == 0` to access `eth_hdr(skb)` even when `skb`'s MAC header was invalid.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `&& par->fragoff != 0` from the guard `if (!(skb_mac_header(skb) >= skb->head && skb_mac_header(skb) + ETH_HLEN <= skb->data))`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that with `par->fragoff == 0`, `eui64_mt6()` could still reach `eth_hdr(skb)` despite an invalid MAC header.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `&& par->fragoff != 0` from the guard `if (!(skb_mac_header(skb) >= skb->head && skb_mac_header(skb) + ETH_HLEN <= skb->data))`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that with `par->fragoff == 0`, `eui64_mt6()` could still reach `eth_hdr(skb)` despite an invalid MAC header.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always hotdrop packets with invalid MAC header bounds in eui64_mt6 instead of only doing so for fragmented packets.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding MAC header bounds in eui64_mt6() was changed by removing the additional conjunction `&& par->fragoff != 0`, so the hotdrop/false return now triggers whenever `skb_mac_header(skb)` is outside `[skb->head, skb->data - ETH_HLEN]` regardless of fragment offset.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packets with an invalid or inaccessible MAC header are now always rejected with `par->hotdrop = true` instead of only being dropped when `par->fragoff != 0`; this prevents malformed packets with bad MAC header positioning from bypassing the safety check on non-fragmented traffic.

grouping_result.intent: Always hotdrop packets with invalid MAC header bounds in eui64_mt6 instead of only doing so for fragmented packets.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by removing the incorrect dependency on fragoff and always validating MAC header bounds before accessing eth_hdr(skb), preventing invalid MAC-header access when fragoff == 0.

candidates.rationale: This condition wrongly gates MAC-header validity enforcement on the packet being fragmented. As a result, when fragoff == 0, invalid MAC header bounds do not trigger hotdrop and later code may access eth_hdr(skb) with an invalid MAC header.
This is the start of the vulnerable bounds-check conditional that is incorrectly combined with the fragoff test, making the MAC-header validation ineffective for non-fragmented packets.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the fragment-offset gate that incorrectly makes MAC-header bounds validation depend on par->fragoff being nonzero. When fragoff == 0, the invalid MAC header path is skipped, allowing later eth_hdr(skb) access with an invalid MAC header.

This is the vulnerable conditional that begins the MAC-header bounds check. In the pre-fix code it is combined with the fragoff test, so the intended validation is not enforced for non-fragmented packets.
